Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.000</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 48 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 2.44.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 22.36.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.214</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 168 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.21.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 5.52.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.700</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 120 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.70.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 2.36.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 49.68.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 19.778</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 162 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 19.78.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.40.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 31.10.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

Correct	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.89.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6. font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 30.286</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 84 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 30.29.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.400</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 120 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.40.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 2.86.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 7.19.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 20.96.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 13.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll. font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.000</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 180 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 2.35.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 21.38.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 1.82.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 13.48.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.533</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 90 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.53.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 41.08.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 14.50.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 8.74.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 40.43.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect

font-weight: bold;">&chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.000</td></tr></tfoot></table><p>You roll a six-sided die 54 times. The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected. Add the six contributions to get &chi;<sup>2</sup>. The total uses unrounded contributions.</p><p>The table below gives chi-square critical values for each probability in the right tail.</p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><thead><tr style="background: #efefef; color: #606060;"><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">Degrees of freedom</th><th scope="col" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: center;">0.05</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">4</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">9.49</td></tr><tr style="background: #f2f5f7;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">5</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">11.07</td></tr><tr style="background: #ffffff;"><th scope="row" style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right; text-align: left; font-weight: normal;">6</th><td style="padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #b8b8b8; text-align: right;">12.59</td></tr></tbody></table><p>Calculated &chi;<sup>2</sup> = 4.00.</p><p>Which one of the following conclusions is supported at &alpha; = 0.05?</p>	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is proven; every face has exactly the same chance on each roll.	Incorrect	Reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Incorrect	The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is disproven; a fair die must give exactly equal counts of all faces.	Incorrect	Fail to reject the null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>); there is not enough evidence that face probabilities differ from 1/6.	Correct

The null hypothesis (H<sub>0</sub>) is that each face has probability 1/6 on every roll.</p><p>Subtract expected from observed, square the difference, and divide by expected.
